facts.text: Dayton, Virginia, is one of the county’s oldest settled communities, incorporated as the second oldest town after Bridgewater.
Shenandoah University began in Dayton as the Shenandoah College and Conservatory of Music, founded in 1875 before moving to Winchester in 1960.
The Dayton Historic District, along with the Daniel Harrison House and Peter Paul House, earned spots on the National Register of Historic Places.
A two‑story stone house built by Daniel Harrison in 1702 remains a private, non‑profit‑owned landmark known as Fort Harrison.
Before 1833, Dayton was called Rifeville, a name that disappeared as the town grew along Cooks Creek.
Visitors can explore the Rocktown History Museum, the Virginia Quilt Museum at Silver Lake Mill, and the historic Fort Harrison within downtown Dayton.
